title: The accounts office can move a due date
summary: The accounts office can now move one student's instalment due date (it used to get a missing permission error).

changes.text: Changing the due date of a student's instalment no longer says the permission is missing. If a late fine has built up you are warned first: keep it (added to Fines) or remove it, for example when the payment was marked late by mistake. Removing is kept on record with your reason and name. Moving a due date for everyone on a fee stays with the administrator.

title: The accounts office can remove a wrong late fine
summary: When a payment is recorded with an earlier date, the accounts office can now remove the late fine itself, with a reason kept on record.

changes.text: Recording a payment or a challan with an earlier date still shows the late fine it would take away. You can now choose either to keep it or to remove it yourself (for example when the payment was marked late by mistake); removing needs a reason, which is kept on record with your name. Moving a due date is unchanged.

title: Father's name in the accounts office; student lookup
summary: The accounts office now sees each student's father (or guardian) wherever it searches, lists or prints fees, can find a student by the father's name or CNIC, and has a read-only Student lookup.

changes.text: Wherever you search or pick a student (Student accounts, Fees list, Refunds, Previous dues, Fines), each student shows the father, e.g. 'Ali Khan s/o Ahmed Khan', so two students with the same name are easy to tell apart. When no father is on record, the main guardian is shown with the relation, e.g. 'Guardian: Sara Bibi (Mother)'.
You can now find a student by the father's name or the father's CNIC (with or without dashes); brothers and sisters come up together.
Fee challans, payment receipts, fee statements and the defaulters list (also its spreadsheet) show the father's name.
Student lookup in the accounts menu: find any student and open a read-only record with their details, father / guardian and fees, and a button straight to their fee account.

title: Late fines are protected; ID cards with a back side
summary: A late fine already built up no longer disappears without a warning, and ID cards have a validity you set and a printed back side.

changes.text: Moving a due date when a late fine has already built up now shows a warning with the amount. The fine so far is kept (added to Fines) and lateness counts again from the new date. Only an administrator can remove it instead, and that is kept on record.

Recording a payment or a challan with an earlier date that would take away a late fine now shows a warning. The fine is kept (added to Fines) and the payment keeps its real date. Only an administrator can remove the fine, with a reason kept on record.
Student ID cards are valid for the number of months set in Settings → Rules → Certificates (6 unless changed); staff cards for a year. Scanning an expired card shows that it has expired.

ID cards now have a back side: the logo, numbered instructions, where to return a found card, and the signature. It prints on the next page, placed for double-sided printing. Write your own instructions in Settings → Look & documents → Back of ID cards.

title: School mode: school fees
summary: For schools: monthly fee vouchers made on the 1st with tuition, transport and annual charges, sibling discounts, admission fees and a fixed late fine.

changes.text: Classes & sections has a Fees tab: set each class's monthly tuition, admission fee and annual charges for the session, add van and bus routes with their monthly fee, and put students on a route.

Each month your child gets one fee voucher on the 1st: tuition, transport (if on a route) and, on the first voucher of the session, the annual charges. It is due on the 10th (set in Settings). Pay it at the bank, by 1Bill or at the school, as before. You are told when it is ready.
Brothers and sisters (same guardian CNIC) get a sibling discount on tuition: 10% for the second child and 20% for the third and later (set in Settings). It is shown on the voucher.

A voucher paid after its due date has a fixed late fine, once (Rs. 200 unless changed in Settings), not a daily one. When you put a new student in a section, tick New admission to charge the class's admission fee.

title: School mode: exams, report cards and promotion
summary: For schools: 1st Term, Mid-Term and Final exams, marks entry by subject teachers, report cards for students and parents, and moving students up to the next class.

changes.text: Classes & sections has a new Exams & results tab: set up the 1st Term, Mid-Term and Final exams, set each subject's total marks (100 unless changed), follow how far marks entry has got in every class, and publish report cards class by class. Students and parents are told when a report card is ready.

Exam marks & report cards: subject teachers enter marks for their sections (tick Absent for a student who missed the paper; it counts as 0). The class teacher also writes remarks and rates skills and behaviour A to D.

Report cards show each subject's marks and grade, the total, position in the section (students with the same marks share a position), attendance, skills and remarks, and can be downloaded as a PDF. Grades follow the board scale; O and A Level classes use the Cambridge scale.

After the Final exam the report card shows the year's result, weighted 20% 1st Term, 30% Mid-Term and 50% Final (changeable in Settings). Promotion moves the students of a class to the next class in the new session: those who passed are ticked, others are kept back or promoted on approval, and Class 8 and 10 students can be placed in their chosen stream.

title: School mode: roll call, homework diary and parent-teacher meetings
summary: For schools: the class teacher's morning roll call with messages to parents, a homework diary, and parent-teacher meetings that parents book.

changes.text: My class: the class teacher marks the section Present, Late, Absent or Leave each morning. Parents of an absent or late child are told at once, in the parent portal and by SMS or WhatsApp. If the class teacher is away, the office can choose a teacher to cover that day.
For school classes the morning roll call is the attendance: each subject's attendance %, admit cards, warnings and the parents' notes use it, and teachers no longer mark attendance in every period.

Homework diary: subject teachers set homework for their sections, with a due date and an optional worksheet (PDF or picture). Students and parents see it at once, and each family gets one message with the day's homework in the evening (the time is in Settings).

Diary & attendance shows your child's homework and a month of attendance. Parent-teacher meetings: when the school sets a meeting day, book a time with the class teacher, and change or cancel it until the day.

Classes & sections now has Roll call (every section's roll call for a day: taken or not, absent and late, open it to correct, set a cover teacher) and Parent-teacher meetings (set a day and minutes per meeting, see bookings, cancel).
Right after changing a first-time password, the portal sometimes showed the change-password page again for a few seconds. It now opens straight away.

title: Combined classes
summary: One teacher can teach the same course to several programs together, e.g. AHS201 for BS Anesthesia and BS Dental, at the same time in the same room.

changes.text: Course section → Overview → Combined class: combine sections of the same course (e.g. section A for BS Anesthesia and section B for BS Dental). They get one teacher and one timetable, with no clash for sharing the teacher and the room. A section without a timetable gets the other's. Each section keeps its own students, attendance, marks and result sheet. A section can be taken out again.

A combined class shows as one class in Attendance and Grading: one list of all its students, each with their program. Attendance and marks are saved to each student's own section, and Submit sends every section's marks.
In a combined class, a timetable slot added, changed or removed in one section is done in all of them, and so is a change of teacher or of the marks scheme.
A combined class has one paper on the datesheet for all its sections: the exam roll, admit cards, clash checks and the number of teachers on duty count every section's students.

title: School mode: classes and sections
summary: A copy can now run a school: classes from Playgroup to Class 12 and O / A Levels, sections with class teachers, subjects and subject teachers.

changes.text: Settings → Institute type: choose School or College / University. A school gets Classes & sections, and the menus use school words (Subjects instead of Courses, Classes instead of Programs). Nothing changes until it is switched on.

Classes & sections → Set up classes: tick Pre-school, Class 1-5, Class 6-8, Matric (Science, Computer Science, Arts), Intermediate (Pre-Medical, Pre-Engineering, ICS, I.Com, F.A.), O Level or A Level, name the session (e.g. 2026-27) and the sections. Each class gets its usual subjects and knows the next class for promotion. Running it again only adds what is missing.

Each section: choose the class teacher, room and seats, and the teacher of every subject. Teachers are told about their new class. Add or remove subjects (optional "choice" subjects for O / A Levels), and add sections.

Put students in a section: they are enrolled in all the class's subjects (and the choice subjects you tick) in one step. A student can move to another section before classes start, taking their subjects along.

title: Exam duty and the exam roll
summary: Put teachers on exam duty with suggestions of who is free, and take a separate attendance in every paper.

changes.text: Datesheets → Duty on each paper: the system says how many teachers are needed (one for every 30 students, changeable in Settings → Exams & results) and lists the teachers who are free at that time first. A teacher with a class or another duty then is marked busy, with the reason. Choose the suggested teachers in one click and mark one as in charge. Duties can be changed until the paper starts.

Exam duties shows the papers you are on duty for. You are told when you are put on duty, taken off, or when the paper's date, time or room changes (also by SMS or WhatsApp when it is switched on in Settings).

Exam roll: on the exam day the teachers on duty mark each student present, late or absent. Only students allowed to sit the paper are listed; students held back by short attendance or unpaid fees are shown apart with the reason. It does not change anyone's class attendance. The exam office can correct it later.
Grading: a student marked absent in an exam paper shows as "Absent" in marks entry for that result type. When creating a datesheet, the exam office can say which result type its marks go into.
Unfair means cases: a teacher on duty can report cheating with a note. The exam office is told and records a decision. Cases are kept on record.
On phones, some wide tables shown as cards had their first line hidden behind a blank bar. Fixed.

title: Task map, notification tones and a message for every change
summary: See who gives tasks to whom on a map, hear a tone when a notification arrives, and get told whenever the office changes something about you.

changes.text: Tasks → Task map: a picture of who gives tasks to whom. Thicker arrows mean more tasks; colours show late, in progress, waiting, done or rejected. Click a person or an arrow to see the tasks. The admin sees everyone; staff see their own.

A notification tone plays in the portal when something new arrives (also in a background tab): the admin picks it for everyone in Settings → Notifications, including long ringtone-like tones and a separate alarm for urgent notices. Phones vibrate longer for urgent notices, and urgent alerts stay on screen until opened.

You are told when the office changes something about you: working hours, attendance corrections, salary, bonus, job role, status, password reset, record details; for students also courses and sections, marks, leave, hostel and fee changes; and everyone in a class when its timetable changes.
Dashboards show only the latest announcement, with View all for the rest.

title: Announcements from teachers and staff
summary: Teachers and staff can write announcements; the admin approves them before anyone sees them. The student home page now starts with the latest announcements.

changes.text: Post an announcement: teachers, heads of department, the principal and other staff write a notice for students (all, by program and semester, or a course section) or for colleagues. It is issued in their own name and job, and goes live once the admin approves it.
Announcements → Waiting for approval: approve and publish, edit first, or send it back with what to change. The writer is told either way and can fix it and send it again.
Home page order: the latest 3 announcements first (new ones marked), then the key numbers, then alerts and deadlines, then today.
Announcements can also be aimed at chosen semesters or course sections.

title: Warnings to students and staff
summary: The admin can give formal warnings with a violation from a list. The 3rd warning within 12 months is final, and the admin or principal decides the action.

changes.text: Warnings: find a student or staff member, choose the violation from the list, write what happened. Each warning counts for 12 months; the 3rd is final. The list of violations can be edited, and a warning given by mistake can be withdrawn with a reason (it stays on record).

Final warnings wait for a decision by the admin or principal: final chance, suspension (cannot sign in until it is ended), expulsion or termination, or a fine. The decision is applied to the person's record.
My warnings: read each warning, confirm 'I have read this', and reply once with your side.
Settings → SMS messages: a switch to also tell a student's guardian about a warning (off unless switched on).

title: WhatsApp messages, with documents
summary: Messages to students and parents can now go by WhatsApp, with the challan, receipt, result card or certificate attached. SMS is used only when WhatsApp fails.

changes.text: Messages from the institute arrive on WhatsApp, with the PDF attached: the challan with a fee reminder, the receipt when a payment is received, the result card with results, and the certificate when it is ready.
A message when a fee payment is received, with the receipt number.
SMS & WhatsApp page: set up WhatsApp (Meta's official WhatsApp Cloud API, or any provider's web link) and send a test. Each message shows whether it went by WhatsApp or SMS.
Settings: two new message switches (payment received, certificate ready).

title: Certificates on request and a monthly report
summary: Students ask for certificates from their portal and download them once approved and paid. The principal gets a monthly report on the 1st.

changes.text: Certificates: ask for a bonafide, character, completion, provisional (result), migration / NOC certificate or a fee clearance letter. Once the office approves it and the fee is paid, download it from the portal. Anyone can check it with the QR code.
Certificate requests: approve (with the fee from Settings, or change or waive it) or refuse with a reason. Anything still outstanding is shown before approving.

Monthly report: fees received and still owed, class attendance by teacher and class, results and pass rates, and staff attendance and leave. A message on the 1st of every month, with a PDF to download; any month can be opened at any time.
Settings has a new Certificates section with the fee for each certificate.

title: A "Today" view for students
summary: The student home page now opens with what matters today: classes, what is due this week and the latest marks.

changes.text: Today: the day's classes (the one running now is highlighted), everything due in the next 7 days (assignments, fee instalments with the consumer number, exams) and the latest marks.
On a phone the number tiles are smaller and the class list shorter, so the day's information fits on the first screen.
Results now has its own button in the phone's bottom bar.
Bigger buttons on touch screens, and the language button no longer gets cut off.

title: اردو — Urdu for parents and students, and fee reminders
summary: Parents and students can use the portal in Urdu, get a reminder before a fee is due, and parents hear on Monday if their child needs attention.

changes.text: Urdu: tap "اردو" on the sign-in page or at the top of any page. The choice is kept on the account and also used for SMS.
Fee reminders 7 days and 3 days before a challan is due, and on the due date, with the amount and consumer number. Only while it is unpaid.
Monday note to parents when a child needs attention: attendance below 75%, low marks so far, or missed assignments. Sent only when something changed.
The parent home page now also lists low marks and missed assignments.
Settings → SMS: switches for the fee reminder and the Monday note to parents.

title: A full portal for parents
summary: Parents now have their own pages for fees, marks, timetable and notices, for each of their children.

changes.text: Fees: what is due, with the challan to download and the consumer number for paying online, and every payment with its receipt.
Marks: quiz, assignment and exam marks in each subject as the teachers enter them, with the total so far.
Timetable & exams: classes for the next two weeks and the exam datesheet with the admit card.
Notices: the institute's announcements for the child's class.
Students now also see each mark as soon as the teacher enters it. The final grade still appears when results are published.
Parents with more than one child switch between them with one tap, and the portal remembers the last one chosen.

title: Fix: link previews on WhatsApp
summary: Shared links to the portal now show the picture card on WhatsApp and other apps.

changes.text: When the portal's link or the "what's new" link was shared on WhatsApp, the preview picture did not appear. It now does.

title: Pay fees online with 1Bill (ready for the bank)
summary: Everything is ready for students and parents to pay fees from any bank app, JazzCash or Easypaisa. It starts working as soon as the bank switches it on.

changes.text: Pay a fee challan through 1Bill from any bank app, JazzCash, Easypaisa, an ATM or a bank counter, using the consumer number on the challan. A late fee, if any, is included, so one payment settles everything.
The receipt appears straight away, with a message in the app and by SMS.
1Bill payments: every online payment of the day, with totals per bank, to match with the bank's statement.
Settings → Fees → Online payment: choose a charge added to each online payment to cover the bank's fee.
Share button next to the version: send the link on WhatsApp or anywhere else. Links to the portal and to "what's new" now show a preview picture with the institute's name.

title: Students to watch, and course feedback from students
summary: Teachers see early which students may need help, and students can say anonymously how each course went.

changes.text: Students to watch: a list of students in your courses whose attendance is below 75%, who have less than half of the marks given so far, who missed 2 or more assignments, or whose fee is overdue for 30 days or more. Each shows why, so you know what to talk about.
Your home page tells you how many students need attention, with a link to the list.

Course feedback: in the last two weeks of each term, students rate each course and teacher from 1 to 5 and can add a comment. It takes about two minutes and is anonymous: answers are saved without names.
Student feedback: see the averages and comments for your courses once their results are published, when at least 3 students answered.
Course feedback overview for the principal, HOD and admin: response rates while the survey is open, and scores for every teacher and course after the term. Admins can change the questions.
Students get a reminder in the app when the survey opens and two days before it closes.
The version number now sits right under the logo in the menu, so it is easy to find, and new versions are celebrated with a little confetti.

title: Version number, What's new, and faster photos
summary: You can now see which version of the system you are using and what changed in each update. Photos load faster.

changes.text: The version number is shown in the menu of every staff portal. Click it to see what's new.
After each update, a short "A new version is here!" message appears once.
A status page shows whether everything is working and which version you are using.
Photos you upload now load faster and take less space, and still look sharp. PDFs and Word or Excel files stay exactly as uploaded.
The system now tidies up after each update, so it keeps running smoothly over time.
Fixed a false warning that made parts of the system look like they had a problem when they were working fine.
Stronger protection for the institute's records, with copies kept safely in a second place every night.

title: Fix: removing a course offering
summary: Deleting a course offering by unenrolling its students works again.

changes.text: Deleting an offering and unenrolling its students showed "An unexpected error occurred", even when no attendance or marks had been entered. It now works. Offerings that already have attendance or marks are still protected and cannot be deleted.

title: Two-step sign-in for administrators, daily money review
summary: Administrator accounts are now protected by a code from a phone app, and every change to money is listed for a daily check.

changes.text: Administrators sign in with their password plus a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator). A trusted device is remembered for 30 days.
If an administrator loses their phone, another administrator can reset their two-step sign-in from Activity → Security.
Activity → Money changes lists every discount, refund, cancelled receipt and fee change, so they can be checked day by day and marked as checked.
A reminder appears at 8 AM when there are money changes from earlier days that nobody has checked yet.
Links in notifications now open the right tab of a page (for example the leave or fines tab).

title: Attendance fine warnings for students and parents
summary: Students and parents can see early whether low attendance will lead to a fine, and how many classes are needed to avoid it.

changes.text: For each subject, students and parents see the attendance band they are in, the fine it would bring, and how many more classes are needed to get back to a safe level.
The admin dashboard shows how many leave requests are waiting and how many students are at risk of an attendance fine.
Sick leave requests need a medical note attached.
The Apply button for leave no longer stays greyed out after a missing-note message.

title: Attendance fines, course rules, staff leave and timetables
summary: A large update: attendance fines by band, rules for which courses a student may take, staff leave requests, printable timetables, safer discounts and a safe nightly copy of all records.

changes.text: Attendance fines per subject by band: 75% and above no fine; 65–74% Rs 3,000; 55–64% Rs 6,000; 45–54% Rs 10,000; below 45% is sent to an administrator to decide. Fines are charged before final exams.
Every Monday, an app message (and SMS if switched on) warns students whose attendance in a subject is in a fine band, with the fine it would mean.
Courses can require earlier courses to be passed first. An administrator can allow an exception.
Each programme has a limit on credit hours per semester (for example 21). An administrator can allow a student to take more.
Staff apply for leave in the app; an administrator approves it and payroll takes it into account. Sick leave is paid up to the yearly allowance set in Settings → Payroll.
Timetables can be printed per class, for the whole institute and per teacher.
Discounts now apply to tuition fee only by default, so other charges (like the student card) are no longer discounted by mistake.
Every night, a safe copy of the institute's records is kept in a second place.

title: Starting point
summary: The system as it was before release notes were kept: admissions, students, staff, courses and results, attendance, fees and receipts, payroll, library, hostel, gate, announcements and the student and parent portals.

changes.text: Email address verification, copies of important emails to administrators, and a friendly "Page not found" page.
